title: GPU MODE Challenge 06: Matmul (fp16 C = A B, 4096x5120x4096 scored)

workload.description: C = A @ B with A (M K) and B (K N) row-major fp16, C fp16. task.yml lists 8 benchmarks (128^3 .. 4096x5120x4096); kernelbot ranks by RankCriterion.LAST, so the score is the LAST case only: m=4096 n=5120 k=4096 (171.8 GFLOP). Correctness is checked on the benchmark inputs too at rtol 1e-5: bit-exact fp16 against cuBLAS.

kernels.strategy: Beauty: one portable 13-line tensor-core kernel -- matrix-multiply-tile-stride, one warp per 16x8 tile, mma.sync m16n8k16, (store-tile (to-half C-tile) ...)
H100: 2wg_deep (2 consumer warpgroups, wgmma m64n256k16, 4-deep TMA ring) after torch `b.t()` copy; A100/L4: 1-warp 64x64 mma.sync, vectorized cp.async (first cut)
H100: 2wg_deep after a Crisp tiled transpose of B (`transpose_b.crisp`, 39 us; torch's `b.t()` copy was 160 us)
A100/L4/B200: 4-warp 128x128 register tile (:warps), flattened 16-byte cp.async walk, await + bar.sync; H100 as v2

takeaways: **The check is bit-exact, so only tensor cores qualify:** `eval.py` re-checks every benchmark input at rtol 1e-5, and with fp16 outputs near 1024 that is an exact match against cuBLAS. A probe (no Crisp) found `mma.sync` m16n8k16 with f32 accumulation summed in K order matches cuBLAS on **all 21M outputs** on H100, A100 and L4, while an IEEE fp32 FMA loop misses 3.7-7% by one ulp. Every Crisp kernel here is a tensor-core kernel with no split-K -- including the small-shape fallback.

**The field is cuBLAS:** #1 / median on 2026-10-27 were H100 205 / 221 us, B200 92 / 114, A100 596 / 683, L4 1990 / 2255 -- most entries call `torch.matmul`. Crisp entries rank H100 41/43, A100 59/60, L4 25/25.

**H100 -- the kernel is the benchmark suite's, the transpose was the surprise:** wgmma reads B K-major and the contest's `b` is (K N) N-contiguous. A per-arm diagnostic on the scored case: the 2wg_deep kernel 306-309 us (~560 TFLOPS, matching the suite's 545 at 4096^3), torch's `b.t()` copy **160 us**. A tiled Crisp transpose (`transpose_b.crisp`, coalesced both sides through a 64x65 shared tile) takes **39 us**: 462 -> 340 us. wgmma transB (on `plan/scramble.md`) would remove it.
**TMA multicast does not help 2wg_deep:** a 2x2-cluster multicast variant was correct and slower (366 vs 309 us); the two-warpgroup tile already reuses each TMA load twice.

**A100 / L4 needed compiler work (endeavour 196):** the Ampere `cp.async` load-tile refused 16-bit tiles (cp.async moves 4/8/16 bytes) -- it now copies 16-byte chunks spread over every thread; the register fit-check refused a 4-warp distributed tile; and `await` on a cp.async barrier lacked the CTA barrier after `wait_group` (2.8% wrong outputs once tiles were shared across warps). A100 6.78 -> 4.96 ms. The remaining gap is operand fragments read from shared memory one 2-byte element at a time (no `ldmatrix`).

**Packaging:** a TMA kernel takes 65 parameters, more than an inline `asm` statement accepts, so this entry loads the PTX through the CUDA driver API (`dlopen` libcuda, `cuModuleLoadDataEx`) with the launch ABI read out of the CUDA hoist. `CU_JIT_THREADS_PER_BLOCK` stands in for `__launch_bounds__`; without it the 288-thread wgmma block failed to launch.

**B200:** Blackwell has no wgmma (its instruction is tcgen05 -- a future endeavour), so the B200 path is the same 4-warp `mma.sync` kernel. Every B200 submission of ours hit the runner's hard timeout (~1570 s), including a plain-CUDA probe with no Crisp in it; no B200 score yet.

beauty_entry.title: One Portable Tensor-Core Kernel
beauty_entry.description: 13-line Crisp matmul that runs unchanged on B200, H100, A100 and L4 and is bit-exact against cuBLAS: `matrix-multiply-tile-stride` walks output tiles and K, `load-tile` stages A and B slices, `mma-accumulate-via-tile` accumulates in f32 on the tensor cores, and `(store-tile (to-half C-tile) ...)` rounds to fp16 as it stores
idioms: matrix-multiply-tile-stride: output-tile walk + K walk + epilogue in one form
make-register-tile: an f32 accumulator that lives in registers
mma-accumulate-via-tile (16 8 16): fp16 tensor-core MMA from staged shared-memory tiles
(store-tile (to-half C-tile) C ...): fused round-to-nearest narrowing on the store (endeavour 196)
